item.title: Re: Corrupted Text
item.content:encoded:
The idea is nice but a bit basic so far and, as said above, have been done before in a similar way. I have some questions that might help give it a more unique spin to it.

Other than being hard to read, what effects this corrupted text has? It spreads so it's akin to a disease, what other symptoms or complications does it cause?
What if it started to affect spoken speech after a while? Maybe even thought process, making the people affected by it to act in a "corrupted" way?

You are still far from the 400 words limit here so you should expand the idea a little more so it will be easier for people to analyse and eventually greenlight it.

item.title: Let's Go on an Adventure! (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious backpack allows individuals to embark into an anomalous dungeon when they wear it. Each of its six pockets can provide the right tool or object for the immediate situation as they progress, necessary as the dungeon itself is filled with dangerous and undiscovered creatures. Though they don’t realize this gauntlet is more preparing them for what’s to come when they reach the final chamber.

+ More Info
Hide

Central Narrative: Discovered in the Mohave Desert by an excavation team, anyone who wears the backpack and walks through the next doorway disappears into an underground passage that changes structure with every embarkment. There are fifty corridors they must traverse to escape, unable to return through each room’s entrance. Each room may entail puzzles or monsters of unknown origin, and adventurers are advised to use each pocket of their pack sparingly because each one only gets one use per journey.
Once they arrive at the fiftieth and final floor, they come across an ancient underground metropolis that now stands abandoned and derelict. The individuals here were all successful explorers that made their city out of the riches of their exploits, however met a gruesome end when a reality-warping chimera they couldn’t defeat followed them to town. The town was buried in an earthquake, the monster trapped with them, and everyone perished under its distorted claws. This backpack was one of the only pieces of gear left intact after this incident.
On the day someone kills the beast, they will find an exit to the surface, and the backpack will lose all anomalous properties. However, nobody who’s taken the backpack has returned alive. The pack reappears where it was taken with no damage, after the wearer has remained dead for at least two hours.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The backpack desires to bring someone strong enough to take down the powerful beast and avenge the lives of the fallen explorers.

Tags: artifact, adaptive, ectoentropic, interactive, portal, safe, sentient, teleportation

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
Sorry to say, but I’m with Metridium on this: there’s no narrative here. You can describe a monster as much as you want, but you need something to give an emotional attachment and narrative thread. Does it escape? Does it have a secret soft spot? Does it have an interesting story of how it was created?

This is gonna sound blunt, what it ultimately comes down to with every article is: “Why should I care?” What reason are you giving for the treader to care about what the Bartender does?

You clearly have a lot of passion for this and I hope to see you take it further.

item.title: Second SCP
item.content:encoded:
This is the second article I wrote after The 13 Correlation, which I'll admit suffers from some first-article frays. This has memetic infiltration, pro career cover-ups, cosmic invasion/apocalypse catalyst, auto-creation of reality through observer effects, a play by play of a rapid Big Rip in the Foundation-verse, how it'd interact with various physical anomalies, a precision redaction about one of my favorite early SCPs that seems creepy in a mystical way.

And to top it off, a spook. I didn't expect to find a face in a quasar.

I think I'm hitting a lot of SCP-genre keynotes here while also bringing some fresh spin. I hope you agree.

LOG-001: “Hello from the Occator Crater. This is Dr. ██████, alongside my fellow researcher Dr. ███ █████. Communication Systems are functional, and we have successfully connected to Station Tau’s primary server. Our mission is the successful extraction of SCP-XXXX. I will also be reporting on a weekly basis the results of our findings.”

LOG-002: “Day 7. Quantities of the fluid seem to get ejected from the chasm out into space continuously. It hasn’t ever stopped since we landed. However, the amount of fluid that gets ejected seems to rise and fall, at least according to our scanning systems. There are currently no correlations involving the increase or decrease in fluid ejection. I will state our findings in our next report.“

LOG-003: Day 14. Me and Dr. ███ █████ have been trying to find any correlations involving the quantity of fluid that gets ejected, to no avail. We’ve tried finding if the presence of Station Tau in orbit changes the ejection level, no connection there. We’ve tried finding if the presence of the Sun changes the ejection level, no connection there. We’ve tried if our presence in Occator Alpha changes the ejection level, no connection there. (We only left Occator-Alpha for two hours, and our life signs are of no concern.) Daily operations mainly consist of me researching the ejection of SCP-XXXX, and Dr. ███ █████ researching methods of extraction.”

LOG-004: Day 22. For some reason, when I tried to upload this log yesterday, all of Station Tau’s communication systems were offline. We are mainly focusing on physical methods to extract SCP-XXXX, but that idea is quite ambitious, considering the fact that we are █ kilometers away from the ejection chasm. However, we are making progress as the days go by, and I am fairly certain that we are closing in on an idea. Another interesting thing that happened two days ago was that while I was walking down the hallway, I passed by another version of myself. He bares no resemblance to Dr. ███ █████, and fully bares resemblance to me. That might be another thing to research in Station Tau. This might be a coincidence, or a lucid dream, but it is something to note.

Log-005: Day 29. Me and Dr. ███ █████ have successfully found a method to extract SCP-XXXX from the ejection chasm. We are planning to build a linear transportation system up to the safe distance of the ejection site, and use a vacuum-like technology to extract SCP-XXXX. Afterward, it will flow through our transportation system, and into our laboratory. In order to prevent SCP-XXXX’s high heat levels from becoming a burden on our research, we have designed a system that will cool anything flowing through the transportation system to approximately absolute zero. That way, we’ll be safe, and so will SCP-XXXX. We have requested a few caches of building material and extra personnel to assist us in construction. On another note, the doppelganger of myself appeared a few times in the past seven days. It doesn’t seem to talk to me, but instead mumbles to itself. I will make a report on what it is trying to say if I find out.

LOG-006: Day 36. Station Tau has greenlit our construction plans, and sent down all of our required materials and labor. They left a message simply stating to keep within the minimum safe distance, and to not construct the vacuum system until their Innovations Laboratory can design a more effective method of extraction. They have also given us permission to cease log uploads until construction is finished. Before I go radio-silent, I want to say that my doppelganger was saying some cryptic messages to itself. For example, it said that “Life is corruption, and I am the purification.” and that “The rising flood matters not in the scale of the universe.” I don’t understand what deeper meaning that had, but I do have a theory. It is entirely possible that ‘the rising flood’ is the ejection of SCP-XXXX, and that this clone is a manifestation of SCP-XXXX’s desires. Perhaps the philosophy majors up in Station Tau can figure that one out. Other than that, construction of the machine will begin posthaste, and I will return when it is complete.

LOG-007: Day 246. Reporting back to Station Tau, because the construction of the machine has been completed. The Innovations Laboratory sent the extraction system just a few days ago, and that was the final part. However, an unfortunate series of events have also occurred. Dr. ███ █████ has died. The cause of death is currently unknown, but he died peacefully in his sleep. Coincidentally, my doppelganger, despite being overt regarding his existence, disappeared the day after Dr. ███ █████’s death. I can’t say whether there is any correlation between my doppelganger’s disappearance and Dr. ███ █████’s death. On the bright side, the D-Class personnel that were sent down from Station Tau have supported me since. Other smaller bases have been constructed around Occator-Alpha. It’s like an entire colony done here, and it will only become larger once we activate our machine, which we dubbed “Extractor-XXXX” and acquire SCP-XXXX. I am sure we can find its origin, and find its containment method. Activation begins tomorrow, and so will my next report. Wish us luck.

The two head scientists in Occator-Alpha gave the theory that there was no correlation in the rising and falling rates of ejection. However, after new findings were reported, a correlation was confirmed. While there are no factors in the ejection rate, the ejection rate has been rising at an identical rate since we’ve arrived. The latest findings from Station Tau have concluded that within ██ years, SCP-XXXX will have the capability to reach Earth. Failure to contain SCP-XXXX within that timeframe will result in an SK “Barren Earth” end-of-the-world scenario.

For this reason, a contingency plan, entitled Operation Theta, was created on 08/2█/202█ and sent to Station Tau, Occator-Beta, and the entirety of the Foundation. This plan contains the instructions for if and when SCP-XXXX’s ejection height is high enough to reach Earth.

item.title: Re: Anger and frustration (scp article)
item.content:encoded:
Was asked to take a look at this.

For the sake of comparison, consider SCP-4057. It sets out to do a very similar thing to what you're talking about but it's a tad "tighter", I guess would be the word. The meme is explained in the narrative, first of all, and it's tied into what happens when the non-anomalous person is contained.

What you've got here is an interesting setup — non-anomalous person in containment — but I'm not sensing a really cohesive story. Where'd this meme come from, why does it only affect the Foundation, why does it become this extreme, why is this person worthy of note, etc.

Here are a few suggestions:

  • "SCP-3178 is seasoning which consists of the composition normally found in factory-made monosodium glutamate with the addition of an unidentified substance." -> "SCP-3178 is a seasoning consisting of factory-made monosodium glutamate and an unidentified substance." It's a minor prose nitpick, but excessive prepositional phrases hurt your clarity and conciseness. I have the same problem, and recommend running your writing through Slickwrite.com to catch it.
  • "the balanced flavour of SCP-3178" is a bit too subjective for my liking. Also, the author can't really know that unless they also tasted it. Maybe say that subjects report the flavor as balanced.
  • "SCP-3178 consumers lose the part of the brain" feels weird. Does that part just cease to exist? It might make more sense to say that it deteriorates
  • SCP-3178-1 feel really disconnected from the rest of the SCP. I'd either remove them or find a way to more smoothly incorporate them.
  • Test logs are good, but a couple of them seem a bit repetitive, maybe remove a couple

On the whole, I think the concept definitely has potential, but there are too many issues for me to give it a +1, so I'm going to make it a non-vote.

Hey blazerboy69420. As someone with a bit more familiarity with the Bosnian War, a lot of your critique here is fairly oblivious to how this story fits in to the themes and conflicts of the war. That time period in former Yugoslavia is famous for a heightened sense of nationalism and disapora, so things like ethnic Croats being born in Canada (thereby not having as direct a connection to Croatia itself), and a bar where ethnicity is not a characteristic one might be killed for are, quite frankly, very salient to the story that's trying to be told here.

Furthermore, a story structure similar to Life is Strange is not uncommon nor something that necessarily needs to be knocked here.

Do you think the Chaos Insurgency just goes recruiting for agents on the fly? Sure I guess the mission stuff would cause a lot of animosity between Sam and Kosta but the fact that Sam somehow joined the CI because of it is literally so unrealistic, not just in-universe but irl. If you're working for the Foundation and you hear there's a splinter group that is actively engaging in attacks on the Foundation, who's firepower and military strength is larger than some countries, and they're actively terminating members of the CI as well, I wouldn't think twice of burying the possibility of me joining the CI to the ground.

The author is in sole control of the story they are telling here. If their conception of the CI is a strapped-for-manpower insurgent group that is desperate for members and is quick to recruit, then they are free to write that, so long as it makes sense in the setting and is sufficiently justified. You are also missing some pretty clear parallels here between the Foundation/CI and US allies/ insurgent groups during the Bosnian War.

If you're reading a pitch that is heavily mired in things you do not understand or have familiarity with, consider not critiquing them if you don't feel you are knowledgeable about the subject.

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX: The Sarkic Uprising of 1947
item.content:encoded:
Okay so a lot to unpack here

Would you like to know more?
Yes

The start of this is incredibly messy and hard to follow. Consider colour-coding your text, especially if you’re using updates, which are usually in blue.

I've read other articles which have crossed out info like this, so why exactly is it hard to read?

See, this is confusing if we weren’t able to remember your labelling system. One option is to simply get rid of xxxx-5 label and mention the Karcist by name. OR convert his label to a PoI-designation, since he’s a separate humanoid entity.

The labelling system seems pretty simple. There are 5 SCP entities, labelled SCP-XXXX-1 through 5. This does not seem very complicated to me. And, as far as I know, the Foundation never refers to anomalous individuals by their birth name other than maybe once in the description or if their properties require them to. Also, he is not a POI, he is an SCP. Simple as that.

You’ve basically given away your entire narrative here, with testing logs, discovery logs and what I assume to be a final interview log with the Karcists all done and wrapped up.

Clearly, I didn't. This description tells you nothing about what happened to the town, where the people are and stuff like that. There are also no testing or discovery logs and there is no final interview with the Sarkics. So evidently I didn't give away my entire narrative as this assumption is entirely wrong.

Notice I still don’t know what these two incidents are referring to. They’re briefly mentioned earlier in the article but you didn’t specify what they were.

Yes…because they would give away the narrative? Something you told me not to do? So isn't that a good thing?

Sorry, but what is this section supposed to be? Is it a log by the researcher? Uncovered documents? An interview with a Historian? I’m highly hesitant to read through a Wikipedia entry (basically an info-dump) as it’s likely to not contain any narrative or character development.

A brief summary of the history of the Cult and the town, says so at the start. And isn't it a good thing to give the reader context for how they got there?

This is the first interesting part of the article, tbh. I always believe character should come first. Consider if you had simply moved this segment to the top of this section. Do you still need all that info when you can simply show what the town is like through the agent’s eyes.

Because if I did that then I would cut out all the information about the cult, its origins, how the US Gov found it and what kind of relationship they had.

It’s basically just producing monsters to fight in wars, yes? Eventually, this leads to conflict with the government (but not the Foundation?)

No. That isn't what happens, of all the cult members they send to war, only one makes creatures to actually attack. The rest are medics. Not to sound rude but statements like this make it sound like you either misread/misinterpreted my article or you did not read the whole thing.

You’d need to majorly restructure this, however, so that it’s more in line with a traditional narrative.

As in a three-act structure? I do that. If you meant more like a normal book then that is impossible to do with this format.

If you’re playing with sarkicism, it’s essential to keep some of the mystery alive as we progress through the article. Make us wonder what’s going on instead of just telling us the facts from the start.

So you weren't even slightly curious about how a town of over 6000 people was reduced to just 5? Other than that, any suggestions for how to keep the mystery alive?

Have the Foundation investigate the claims and forget the US government, I feel.

Then the entire point of this story is lost. The whole point is that this SCP is supposed to show you WHY the government can't just handle this and WHY the UIU is so underfunded. If the Foundation simply looked into all of this then all that is lost. Furthermore, the Foundation would not do what the US gov did when dealing with the cult, so the story would need radical alterations which I do not want to make.

item.title: Ocean's Cell
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type:SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:SCP-XXXX is a wormhole of anomalous nature located on a deep-sea level, it has the appearance of a 2 km deep round trench. Any organism or structure that trespasses it fully will shrink down to a 0.001% of its original size. Set hole will unexplainably start to inhale during 2-3 hours specially during June, July and August.

This wormhole is connected to SCP-XXXX-A, (a standard plastic family pool) which is property of a Caucasian family located in ████████████████. After diving 1 km into the pit 1 km, the walls will start to resemble the tube of a filter pump. Once entering SCP-XXXX-A through the filter hole, it appears to have a size of 2000km long, 1500km wide and 1000km high from set perspective.

SCP-XXXX-A possesses a thin plastic layer partially covering the surface, aswell as many human and insect organic tissues of massive size floating at the surface or underwater, and a chlorine dispenser originally used as a safe base to monitor the surroundings.

There are 5 inhabitants in SCP-XXXX, labeled SCP-XXXX-1 through 5. These are 4 caucasian human individuals (2 male and 2 female) and a canine creature (from the Canis lupus familiaris race). These entities only appear during certain daytime hours in the summer season, and communication with these individuals at first was impossible and dangerous.

The wormhole's origin was later discovered by reaching the surface and achieving connection. The foundation sent a team towards the location and acquired the anomaly, as well as capturing the family to interview them about the item. The pool was brought into a containment cell and since then it has been studied its size-shifting properties.

Central Narrative:During the first encounter with the wormhole, the foundation sent multiple teams to enter SCP-XXXX. Once arriving to the other end, they were amazed at the ocean despite being empty and confusing. Other than that, no other anomalies were present until the appearance of SCP-XXXX-1 to 5, which were a threat to the team since the entities weren't aware of them, causing many casualties. After receiving information about the location of SCP-XXXX,it was successfully contained.

Hook-Attention-Grabber:This anomaly is simple, a wormhole that connects the ocean to a pool. However, the most interesting part is the many changes this SCP goes through the more understood it is, until completely containing it. If done correctly, it should be classified as a Euclid, then reclassified Keter, and finally Safe.

Additional Notes:This SCP has a lot of layers and changes. It may be a bit confusing due to everything it presents so i'll need to do it correctly. I'm fairly new here so I understand if there are problems with the idea, so please tell me since i want to improve on this concept.

/scp-5492 (no title) by CocoaIzBlu deleted at -20 and three votes.

SCP-5492 is a speaker-like object produced somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877. Object#: 5492 is a half-rotten spruce cuboid, plated with metal speakers made with aluminium. Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye.

Feedback ported:

[+] from DoctorSasbo
– hide block

It's really unfortunate that everybody is downvoting this without actually commenting suggestions to help it. Here's my two cents:

The biggest issue with this imo is the prose:

  • "immensely scant amount of room, and heaps of soundproof foam" is not clinical enough for an official document. Try saying "an enclosed space insulated by soundproof foam", or state the measurements if you want to drive home the extent of it
  • "due to the lack of knowledge on SCP-5492" - If it's being researched, we already know there's a lack of knowledge, so the phrase is redundant
  • "somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877" - Firstly, I think you meant "sometime" instead of "somewhere." Secondly, if you have that specific of a year, it doesn't make sense to add uncertainty by saying "probably." Finally, you might want to briefly say where it's from/was found.
  • "Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye" could just be "It is predominantly white." You're spending a lot of words elaborating on something that could be written more concisely.
  • "at the first glances… teeth to commit suicide." is too long of a sentence, try breaking it up into multiple sentences so the reader can more effectively process it
  • ""the noise is so dreadful it's better to die than live to remember the horror" - Which was said by a test subject." I get what you're going for, but it comes off as kinda flat and cliche. You might want to flesh it out a bit more with an interview log, so you can go more in detail about the effects on the subject.
  • "the unfathomable entity" doesn't fit the clinical tone. It's SCP-5492.
  • "When the surviving Subject made it out of the containment he was insane and instead of being suicidal he was critically homicidal instead." Instead of just saying he's homicidal, try describing what he did i.e. stab researchers, torture fellow D-class, etc.

Overall, I think this is a workable concept, but the execution is severely lacking. Tighten up your prose, and try to elaborate more on what actually happens so you can show instead of just telling. Hope this helps!

Forum thread: Intergalactic blackmail

I'm pretty sure that The Serpent's Hand, not being a bunch of fools, will most likely not attempt to breach keter-class SCPs. So far from what I heard, the only SPCs that they breach/steal are safe or thaumiel. They might breach containment of keter-level SCPs only to serve as a distraction to steal other, safer SCPs and anomalous items, but they don't outright break them out of the facility because, again, they aren't stupid. They don't want to end the freakin' world, they just want rights for anomalies, namely humanoid ones that don't pose much of a threat compared to other anomalies. Hell, they even work from the Wonderer's Library, which, in of itself, would be a Safe-class entity just by how it is described (none of the entities within ever go outside of the Library, and none of them attack humans so long as they don't damage the Library or the entities).

The SCP foundation isn't entirely a moral organization, considering that they need to have an ethics committee to keep themselves in check (though highly unethical things are still done to test subjects and anomalies from time to time).

Like Dr. Gears said it,

The Black Queen (or Queens) is (or are), for all intents and purposes, human beings with human emotions leading human lives.

Plus, getting her father back isn't even the only motive behind the Black Queens' actions (have you even read the article on the Serpent's Hand Themselves, or went onto The Wanderers' Library wiki? I bet you haven't.

I would also like to mention that the SCP Foundation is perfectly capable of cleaning up in the event that the Serpent's Hand attacks a site and causes the breach of a keter-class anomaly.
